Where the sources leave gaps, some backgrounds are illustrative reconstructions. Official card art carries the interpretation of the artists who created it; we admire that work, and do not claim every image depicts this exact moment. ## The summons

Halcyon had banished Yawgmoth. Now it summoned him back—and left him to walk.

He reached a rocky overlook above Pilgrim Way, the highway across the desert to the Thran capital. Skyships passed overhead with grain and ale. The Elder Council had called him from exile to treat Glacian, Halcyon's greatest artificer, but sent no vessel for the physician himself.

For five years Yawgmoth and two hundred followers had lived beyond the empire, studying disease among peoples the Thran cast aside. His exile followed a century of civil conflict, reframed as a political contest: artificers sought improvement through machines; eugenicists studied the body's living mechanisms. When Halcyon's imperial party prevailed, the eugenicists were expelled.

Yawgmoth held that disease arose from material causes: organisms invading the body, processes gone wrong. The Council had condemned that work as unorthodox. Now Glacian's illness had defeated the healers, and magic only worsened it.

The summons gave Yawgmoth entry to the capital and a chance to prove his science. His pride is plain: he was pleased the empire needed him, and meant it to remember.

## The threshold

The road climbed toward Halcyon's gate. White marble rose above the narrow passage, and carved figures occupied niches in its columns. An artificial stream crossed the threshold; visitors washed the desert dust from their feet before entering.

Rebbec came to meet Yawgmoth. She had argued for the revocation of his banishment and had come from the infirmary, where her husband remained gravely ill. At the gate, she washed the road from Yawgmoth's feet herself.

Welcome ended at the infirmary door. Glacian had suffered for a year. His disease, phthisis, resisted treatment, and magic made it worse. Yawgmoth examined him and took samples. He found many small organisms, but none explained the illness.

Removing the powerstone from Glacian's chair had allowed some lesions to recede. It had not cured him. Yawgmoth's first work in Halcyon therefore began with an absence: the cause remained hidden, while the man he had been summoned to save continued to decline.

Rebbec placed him near Glacian. The cause remained hidden.

## The descent

Glacian's illness suggested a trail. The man who had stabbed him came from the Caves of the Damned, the sealed underworld beneath Halcyon. If the attacker carried the disease, Yawgmoth reasoned, the caves might lead him toward its source.

Once a penal colony, the caves held criminals sent below to labor in darkness. The prisoners overthrew their overseers. Halcyon failed to retake the caverns, sealed all but one entrance, and continued sending people down.

Yawgmoth prepared for the descent with lanterns, instruments, and weapons. At the guarded entrance, he killed the keeper Dorin and spared a child who became his guide. The choice did not make the journey safe. It carried him farther into a place the city feared and had chosen not to see.

The child led him to a cavern where thousands huddled around small fires. They were quarantined; all had the sickness. Yawgmoth asked for the man from the mana rig who had stabbed Glacian.

The child gave him a name: Gix.

## Two patients

By the next morning, Glacian and Gix sat in the same infirmary alcove. Phthisis had reduced both men, though Gix had improved since Yawgmoth found him near death in the caves.

Yawgmoth treated them together, taking samples, applying salves, placing strips of metal beneath the skin, and recording the results. The method was clinical; its effect was cruel. Gix was strapped into his chair. Yawgmoth did not spare pain when he believed the experiment required it.

Glacian understood the danger of being useful. The Council that expelled Yawgmoth now offered assistance, needing a cure and fearing civil conflict. It had given authority to a man it once cast out.

The disease still resisted a cure. Yet Yawgmoth had found one important relation: contact with powerstones made the illness worse. For the physician, each patient was evidence. For Glacian and Gix, the evidence was being gathered from their bodies.

## The rising foundation

That day, Yawgmoth left the infirmary for the public raising of the Thran Temple's suspended foundation. Rebbec had designed the great plane of powerstones, a work of engineering and spectacle above Halcyon.

As the foundation lifted, its stones scattered light. Rebbec stood upon it. Yawgmoth crossed the upper city, leapt from the Council Hall dome, and landed beside her. They embraced, laughing. Rebbec credited all who had made it possible.

Below, Glacian could not endure the powerstone glare. The temple's rising presence aggravated his lesions, and he asked to be taken back down.

Then came the test. Yawgmoth laid the crimson powerstone against Gix's chest. The lesions darkened; skin cracked. Rebbec reached for the stone, and Yawgmoth caught her wrist. She warned him not to forget the people for whom he sought a cure. He released her. At the door, he looked back and answered with a single word: Yes.

Below, Gix was climbing toward Halcyon with hundreds of the damned behind him. The news he carried was meant not for the damned, but for the demons above.

The temple rose. The condemned were coming up.

summary: After five years beyond the Thran Empire, Yawgmoth is summoned to Halcyon to treat Glacian. The return brings him into a city divided by sickness, political fear, and the powerstones its people depend upon.
